questions: Did this eyelid drooping start suddenly, within the past 72 hours?
Have you experienced any new double vision along with the drooping eyelid?
Have you had a severe headache or eye pain in the days before this started?
Have you noticed any weakness or numbness in your arm, leg, or face on either side?
Have you had any recent infection, like a cold or sinus infection, or a history of diabetes?
Does the eyelid drooping get worse later in the day or after using your eyes for a long time?
Does the drooping improve after you rest or sleep?
Have you noticed any difficulty swallowing or slurred speech?
Do you have any family history of autoimmune diseases like thyroid problems or myasthenia gravis?
Have you had any drooping in both eyelids at the same time?
When did you first notice this drooping - was it weeks, months, or years ago?
Have you ever had eye surgery or any trauma to that eye?
Do you wear contact lenses?
Have you ever noticed that one of your pupils looked smaller than the other?
Do you feel like your left eye looks "staring" or more open than the right eye?
Have you ever been told your left eye looks different or unusual?
Have you noticed any blurriness or changes in vision in either eye?
Do you have any dryness, grittiness, or tearing in either eye?
When you look downward slowly, does your left eyelid follow smoothly or does it seem to hang up or move slower than expected?
Have you ever had your thyroid tested or been told you have any thyroid problems, even if it was years ago?
Are you currently taking any medications, including over-the-counter supplements or thyroid medications?
Does anyone in your family have thyroid problems or any eye conditions?
Have you ever had any treatment for this eyelid appearance or been evaluated by an eye doctor before?
orders: Bright light / dim light anisocoria assessment (document pupil size difference in bright versus dim conditions)
Measurement of right upper eyelid fissure height in millimeters
Assessment of eyelid excursion (levator function) on the right side
Measurement of proptosis using Hertel exophthalmometry (both eyes in millimeters)
Assessment of extraocular movements (ductions and versions)
Assessment for lid lag on downgaze (asking patient to look down while observing upper eyelid movement)
Serum TSH, free T4, and free T3
Anti-thyroid peroxidase (anti-TPO) and TSH receptor antibodies (TRAb)
Ice test on the left upper eyelid (applying ice pack for 2 minutes, then measuring for any improvement in retraction - improvement would suggest myasthenia gravis)
Assessment of right upper eyelid excursion (levator function) in millimeters
Measurement of bilateral eyelid fissure widths in primary gaze
Orbital MRI with fat suppression and contrast (to evaluate extraocular muscles, orbital fat, and rule out structural lesion causing eyelid retraction)
Forced duction testing of the left eye (to assess for any mechanical restriction)
served: lid position and measurement (MRD1 both sides)
